title: 2018 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 2018 FIFA World Cup, staged in Russia from 14 June to 15 July, was the first edition held in Russia and the first ever hosted in Eastern Europe. Thirty-two teams were drawn into eight groups of four, with the group stage feeding a single-elimination knockout bracket of the round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final, 64 matches in all. It was also the first World Cup to deploy the Video Assistant Referee, or VAR, system, marking a technological turning point for the tournament. More than 3 million spectators attended across the 64 matches, an average of roughly 47,000 per game.

The group stage produced an early shock when defending champion Germany was eliminated, its earliest World Cup exit since 1938. The defining story of the knockout rounds belonged to Croatia, the smaller nation reaching its first ever World Cup final on a run anchored by midfielder Luka Modrić. France advanced to meet them at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium on 15 July.

In the final, France defeated Croatia 4–2 to claim its second World Cup title, after 1998, leaving Croatia as runner-up in its maiden final appearance. Among the French scorers was Kylian Mbappé, who at 19 became the first teenager to score in a World Cup final since Pelé in 1958 and was named Best Young Player. The victory also meant France became the fourth different European nation to extend the continent's run of four consecutive World Cup titles, following the European winners of 2006, 2010 and 2014.

Individual honours were spread widely. England's Harry Kane finished as top scorer with six goals, while Luka Modrić was awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player. In the third-place play-off, Belgium defeated England to secure third place, and Belgium goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois won the Golden Glove.
